inverseSummary: With known mass and calibrated complex input–output response, the two synthetic natural frequencies are recovered and pass held-out numerical checks. Incorrect gain and multimode controls fail. An unconstrained frequency-dependent receiver still passes as a different oscillator, including at the same known mass. Stability and causality alone do not remove this ambiguity. No Earth parameters were inferred.

protocol: Define the claim first: local fitted peak, common cavity pole, amplitude change or global event. Preselect station, channel, band, UTC interval, baseline and statistical decision rule.

Obtain raw or calibrated spectral records with sensor orientation, gain and phase response, clock accuracy, sampling, windowing, missing-data and clipping flags. Preserve immutable source bytes and permission to reuse them.
Use a matched seasonal/local-time baseline, a documented noise/source model, uncertainty propagation, dependence-aware statistics and correction for selected windows or multiple modes.
Compare independent calibrated stations for a global claim. Model lightning geography, receiver response and interference before attributing a shift to a changed cavity.

Validate the inverse method on a controlled low-energy mechanical or electrical analogue with a measured input and at least two distinct held-out frequencies. Distinguish bench validation from observational Earth identification.

For any energy-collection proposal, measure source work, storage changes, dissipation and load power over a complete cycle; report uncertainty and a no-load control. Static magnetic density does not supply a power estimate.

edges.reason: A Euclidean free-wave estimate does not directly control a curved, lossy, driven inverse cavity problem.
An asymptotic SAT theorem needs a concrete reduction and benchmark before claiming computational benefit.
Announced continuum existence has a different scope; physics proof artifacts are not publicly auditable here.
The primary SR paper distinguishes forced peak frequencies from cavity eigenfrequencies; our model tests the general nuisance mechanism.
Synthetic ambiguity controls identify which calibrated input–output assumptions a bench test must expose.
No imported theorem presently closes the experimental calibration or statistical inference requirements.
The current strong-coupling certificate is not uniform along g(a)→0; continuum and physical-gap obligations remain.
Kp measures geomagnetic activity and cannot confirm or exclude a Schumann-frequency anomaly.
A synthetic response is not a calibrated station record or a matched anomaly baseline.
Solar-wind-associated apparent-frequency changes and three-station uncertainty controls already have a published precedent.
A next cycle needs a distinct question, usable data/calibration and an assumptions-matched benchmark before execution.

criteria: State the exact proposition or measurable improvement, with domains, units, observables and nuisance assumptions.
Map it against the nearest primary theorem or experiment, including sections, assumptions, dates and actual reading depth. Search failure is not novelty evidence.
Identify a residual gap that the cited work does not already solve. Separate theoretical novelty, empirical extension and useful replication.
Secure the needed dataset or apparatus calibration; document licenses, raw bytes, uncertainty and what cannot be reproduced.
Predeclare an assumptions-matched baseline, untouched evaluation cases, meaningful success metric and rejection/stop criteria.
Freeze an advisor go/no-go decision before any next three-round cycle. Keep the existing cycle closed and preserve its superseded failures.
